chapter: Arthur Gibbs, Savoy Ballroom and recording sessions
title: Recording Knocking the Jug with Louis Armstrong
summary: With Jack Teagarden and Kaiser Marshall, an unwritten blues session produced Knocking the Jug and Muggles.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Yeah. In 1929 you recorded with Louie Armstrong. How did that come about?
Right. Well, the Louie -- Louie Russell, the piano player, had the band for Louie. So Jack Teagarden -- Louie said, called me up, said, Hap, said, got a

you, I said, we called him Pops session for (unintelligible) Okay, Pops (unintelligible), called him Okay, Louie. So we have a -- come on down -- studio. We went down that morning, and there ain't nothing written printing out, and the blues, you know, Pops said, we're going to play a little blues. Okay. So what do you make of them? After we'd made the thing, he called it "Knocking the Jug."
Well, what the title came from, Louie didn't drink, very little. Louie didn't drink much. But --
Well, he used to smoke a good deal.

Well, he smoked (unintelligible), but Jack Teagarden and I would drink. Pop, he didn't drink much, Pops Faster. And Kaiser was on drums. Well, he did a little bit drinking while talking. And this guy that played the guitar, the bass guitar, well, he died too, used to -- Italian fellow, very good guitar player. And that was "Knocking the Jug" and Knuckles. [Eddie Lang]

The one side is "Knocking the Jug." That was the most outstanding, but the collector's item -- and "Muggles" was on the other side. So that's how we got "Knocking the Jug" because we done knocked -- he calls it, hey, man, let's knock our jug, and that means we're going to get a little drink.
Well, in the books it says that on that session they made another tune called "I'm Going to Stomp Mr. (unintelligible) Henry Lee."
"Stomp Mr. (unintelligible) Henry Lee."
That was never put out then.
It never was.
What was the matter with that tune?
I don't know. That was Jack Teagarden's number too.
Oh, maybe you were knocking the jug too hard.
Maybe --
(Laughter)

-- because (unintelligible), I know, 'Knocking the Jug,' Muggles Stomp with Henry Lee. I don't know where that -- whether I heard the (unintelligible) playback. It was nice. In my estimation, it was pretty nice.
Well, I mean it's nothing that -- evidently they didn't keep it because --
They didn't.
-- by now they'd have found that (unintelligible).
(Simultaneous remarks)
'Knocking the Jug was very good, though.
Yeah, they're considered one of the good collector's items. (unintelligible) played those over at the WRVR.
Nice dance record.
